conservation_status.description: The species is endemic to the centre-west and southwest Portugal where it has an area of occupancy of 400 km². It is a rare species that is only found at three locations with declining populations. Several subpopulations have not been found again. The main threats are competition with other species, cleaning of roadsides or Eucalyptus plantations, and widening of existing communication networks. It is therefore classed as Endangered.
